title: Sowing broccoli microgreens
subtitle: How to fill, sow, and start the blackout phase for a broccoli microgreen tray
excerpt: Broccoli is one of the most reliable microgreen crops to sow. Small round seeds, no pre-treatment needed, and fast germination. Fill a 25 cm tray, scatter seed at 15 to 20 g, press into contact with the medium, and blackout for two to three days.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fine-textured, low-fertility growing medium designed for germination. Seed compost has smaller particles than multi-purpose compost, which helps seeds make even contact with the medium surface. Use it for microgreen trays rather than multi-purpose compost.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. In darkness, germinating seeds direct energy into pushing the shoot upward rather than greening. The shoots reach 2 to 3 cm before the cover is removed and the tray is moved to light.

content.text: Broccoli is one of the easiest microgreen crops to sow. The seeds are small and round, no pre-soak is needed, and germination is reliable at room temperature. The method here applies to most small brassica seeds.

One 25 cm × 25 cm growing tray. A second tray of the same size for the blackout cover. Seed compost. A watering can or jug. Broccoli seed: 15 to 20 g per tray. A flat piece of card or the base of the second tray for pressing.

Step 1: pre-dampen the compost. Mix water into the seed compost before filling the tray until it holds together when squeezed but doesn't drip. Starting with damp medium avoids having to water after sowing, which risks washing seed off the surface.
works better than multi-purpose compost. The finer texture helps seeds lie flat and sprout evenly.
Step 2: fill the tray to within 1 cm of the rim. Level and firm the surface gently.

Step 3: scatter seed at 15 to 20 g per tray. Hold the seed over the tray from 15 cm up and scatter with a pinching motion, moving systematically across the tray in rows to get even coverage. Broccoli seed is small; it distributes well with a little care.

Step 4: press. Place the flat base of the second tray or a piece of card on the seed and press down firmly across the whole surface. This presses each seed into contact with the medium and significantly improves the germination rate.
: stack the second tray on top with a light weight. Place anywhere at room temperature. Broccoli germinates in two to three days; check for upright 2 to 3 cm shoots before moving to light.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with broccoli microgreens.

items.symptom: Patchy germination with dense areas and bare spots
items.fix: Scatter in systematic rows across the tray. Scatter from higher above the surface (20 cm) so seed spreads more widely on impact.

items.cause: Seed not in contact with the medium, or room too cold.
items.fix: Press more firmly after scattering. Confirm room temperature is above 15°C.

items.symptom: Medium dries out during the blackout phase
items.cause: Pre-dampening was insufficient, or the room is very dry.
items.fix: Bottom-water the tray: pour 1 to 2 cm of water into an outer tray and set the sown tray inside it for 10 minutes, then remove. Do not pour water over the seed surface.
